# C45 — Operational Parity

<a id="0"></a>
## #0 — The technical claim locates its consequence

Operational Parity applies when software claims to instantiate a philosophical or formal distinction. The claimed difference must have an identifiable operational locus and a consequence that inspection or a meaningful test can discriminate. A philosophical distinction can remain valid without being encoded; parity governs the technical promotion.

A paradigm representation gives this criterion a definite case. If a system claims not merely to *represent* its paradigm but to make that paradigm inspectable and refinable, the claim must identify **which enacted mediating relation can be changed through the representation and what later operation changes with it**. A map that is accurate but causally disconnected from the field it maps may be valuable; it has not yet established paradigm-level Epi-Logos.

<a id="1"></a>
## #1 — The distinction has an operative address

Name the operation carrying the distinction: retrieval, storage, routing, permission, exclusion retention, evaluator, collaboration or return. A new label on an unchanged process supplies no such locus. Through [epistemic cultivation](../A33-Epistemic-Cultivation-Operational-Parity.md), an inherited field yields a selected branch under a stabilising rule. Retaining a consequential counter-reading keeps the result answerable; its effects become conditions of later work and its completed form can return into revisable data.

For a paradigm claim, add the relation between **explicit articulation and enactment**. What does the representation point to in the live field? Is that relation attributable? Can a relevant feature of the enactment be changed through the articulated object? Does the changed field then alter what is retrieved, permitted, judged, expressed, built or materially executed? If no such path exists, the representation may disclose the paradigm to a reader while remaining operationally external to the paradigm it describes.

<a id="2"></a>
## #2 — The comparison activates the difference

A comparison must preserve or account for the relevant conditions while testing the claimed difference. It must also put the distinction to work. Removing a permission-checking route from a task that never requests a restricted action need not change its result. That agreement does not establish that permission has no operational force; the task did not exercise the distinction. A discriminating comparison includes a case in which the relevant condition changes what the system can do. A proposed deferential comparison puts consequential decisions with and without disclosure of origin, aperture, exclusions, confidence, counterclaim and undecidable remainder alongside one another. The outcome concerns delegation, correction and answerability, not the frequency of humility words. This is a proposed real-function comparison, not a result already demonstrated.

A constructed source-return test makes the sequence concrete. Begin with a route planner whose retained map marks a gate passable. Supply the same correction, task and map state to two otherwise comparable versions. One displays the correction without a route into the map; the other can apply it to the map used in later planning. Inspect the map state, the correction's authority and the next route. The first may produce an eloquent acknowledgement while selecting the old path. The second must be shown to inherit the corrected condition in the decision said to depend on it.

A difference between two outputs alone does not identify its cause. Variations in other inputs, permissions or generation must be held fixed where possible or accounted for by repeated, attributable comparisons. Conversely, if the first version routes the information through some other active channel, it was not a read-only control for the claimed operation. The comparison has to follow the actual path of influence rather than the interface's label.

The same logic applies to Epi-Logos. Compare an explicit paradigm representation that is **read-only** with one whose authorised changes can revise a governing relation—source, permission, evaluator, composition, material binding or containing frame—while task and other relevant conditions are held as stable as the test permits. The relevant result is not that users report the second interface as “more transparent.” It is whether a returned distinction produces a traceable change in subsequent operation and whether that change can itself be inspected and contested.

<a id="3"></a>
## #3 — The criterion becomes answerable

The metric's own source and gauge belong inside the claim. A test can detect compliance with a stated criterion while the criterion excludes the affected reality it purports to serve. The [arbiter](../A24-Arbitration-and-the-Usurpation-of-Measure.md) has a jurisdiction and an inherited measure; that measure must remain open to regard and return. Exposing it is different from certifying the metric as the whole.

An evaluator's approval states success under its criterion. A claim that the criterion itself became revisable needs evidence of which governing rule changed, how the change was authorised and which later act inherited it. The old evaluator can remain useful for a bounded comparison; its approval alone does not establish those further events. The before-and-after operation must become available to inspection, with a route through which affected sources, users, collaborators or material consequences can contest the revision. This is a relational test inside the field, with its own declared conditions of observation.

<a id="4"></a>
## #4 — The consequence returns to its actual office

Summing terms and dividing one by another perform different acts. An [accountable ratio](../A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md) keeps the terms and their comparison available for reckoning even where the same numbers recur. Equality of numerical results does not make those operations interchangeable. Operational parity applies the same demand to philosophy and code. If a formal or philosophical distinction is said to motivate a feature, identify the technical operation corresponding to that distinction and the consequence by which its presence or absence can be discriminated. A successful implementation check establishes that stated operational consequence. The metaphysical argument retains its own warrant; the implementation neither borrows nor cancels it.

The six-product field gives paradigm-level parity concrete loci. [Central](../products/S0-Central.md): did meaningful ground/source change? [Actuation](../products/S1-Actuation.md): did the judgment or evaluator relation change? [AIKit](../products/S2-AIKit.md): did availability, relevance, permission or selection change? [Factory](../products/S3-Software-Factory.md): did evidence precipitate into changed developmental form? [Workcell](../products/S4-Workcell.md): did the material world, binding or observed consequence change? [QL](../products/S5-Quaternal-Logic.md): did the relation among frames or the containing reading change? A claimed “paradigm update” must name its locus rather than invoke the whole sixfold rhetorically.

<a id="50"></a>
## #5→0 — A finding changes the next inquiry

A named distinction becomes [an accountable reckoning](../../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/encounter-region-name-count/WHOLE-FIELD-encounter-region-name-count.md#count-to-account) when its criterion, source and consequence can be examined through the retrieval, retention, evaluation or action said to carry it. Comparison must distinguish an implementation error, an inadequate operational mapping and a test that cannot discriminate the claim. Keeping those outcomes separate allows revision without making either technical success or failure a blanket verdict on the philosophical field.

The source-return test makes the three findings concrete. A correction that never reaches the intended map can expose a broken implementation. A corrected map with no bearing on the decision can expose a mistaken claim about what actually governs selection. An unchanged route in a task that never uses the gate can expose an inadequate test. [Epistemic Cultivation](C46-Epistemic-Cultivation.md) retains the finding in the next revision; [Deferential Intelligence](C47-Deferential-Intelligence.md) lets the encounter reach the receiving model or governing condition. Parity succeeds as a discipline when it can revise its own criterion without erasing what the prior test showed.

For the Expression programme, the negative test is especially useful. Rendering the paradigm as glyph, text, image, field or transition establishes **expression**. It establishes **Epi-Logos** only where manipulating or contesting that expression can return to the governed structure and where the changed structure changes a later act. Conversely, a non-visual configuration change can satisfy the operational return without satisfying the expressive ambition. The two accomplishments should be measured separately before they are joined.
